etymology: Compound ideograph: a garment (衣) worn fur-side out — the outside face of things: surface, exterior; what is displayed: a chart, a table.
mnemonic: Wear the coat fur-out and everyone sees your outside — おもて, ヒョウ. 発表 is turning your inside out on purpose.

etymology: Compound: grain (禾) + 少 'tiny' — originally the hair-thin awn at the grain's tip; adopted for the thinnest slice of time: the second.
mnemonic: Time shaved as fine as the whisker on a rice grain — ビョウ. 一秒: one awn's worth of your life.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person bent over a cowrie (貝) — shouldering a debt: to bear a burden; the one who carries the loss: defeat.
mnemonic: Bowed under the moneylender's shell — まける. To lose is to carry; 勝負 asks who walks away upright.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 咅 (phonetic ブ) + city (阝) — one district of the town: a section, department; in school, the club.
mnemonic: The town carved into wards, your name on one — ブ. 全部 is all the wards at once; 部活 the ward you sweat for after class.

etymology: Phono-semantic: altar (示/ネ) + 畐 'jar filled to the brim' (phonetic フク) — abundance granted at the altar: blessing, good fortune.
mnemonic: The offering jar comes back from the altar full — フク. 福 is what spills over; 幸福 when it spills on you.

etymology: Pictograph read as a balance at rest — or duckweed lying flat on water: level, even, calm.
mnemonic: The scale's beam dead level, nothing trembling — たいら, ヘイ. 平和 is that stillness scaled up to nations.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 反 'flip' (phonetic ヘン) — walking the road flipped around: to return something, to reply.
mnemonic: Same road, reversed footage — かえす. 返事 is words making the return trip.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 方 'direction' (phonetic ホウ) + 攵 'hand with stick' — driven off toward the horizon: to release, let go, banish.
mnemonic: A tap of the stick and it bolts for open country — はなす. 放送 releases voices into the air on purpose.

etymology: Compound ideograph: an order (口) spoken from above the assembly (亼) to one kneeling (卩) — the command; and the allotted span it decrees: life, fate.
mnemonic: The decree read out while you kneel: this much time, this path — いのち. Life, in the old script, is an order you receive.

etymology: Pictograph: a face framed by its outline with one eye showing — the face; a mask; any facing surface or aspect.
mnemonic: An eye peering from inside the frame of a Noh mask — メン. 場面, 画面, 真面目: scenes, screens and the earnest face you keep on.

etymology: Compound ideograph: marching (彳) with a weapon (殳) — pressed into service: duty, office; the part one is assigned: a role.
mnemonic: Shouldering the spear because your number came up — ヤク. On stage the draft is kinder: 役 is just your role.

etymology: Phono-semantic: liquid (氵) + 由 (phonetic ユ) — the slick liquid: oil.
mnemonic: A liquid with its own agenda (由): it floats, it clings, it burns — あぶら. 醤油: the oil-like sauce that runs Japan.

etymology: Origin debated — a gourd putting out its sprout, or a wick rising from a lamp; since antiquity it has meant the 'whence': cause, reason, via.
mnemonic: The sprout shows where the vine came from — ユ. 理由 is the sprout of any claim; 自由 is growing wherever you please.

etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 斿 'banner streaming, child beneath' (phonetic ユウ) — drifting like a flag on the wind: to roam, to play.
mnemonic: A kid trailing a streamer, going nowhere in particular, perfectly — あそぶ. 遊園地: the industrial complex of exactly that.

etymology: Pictograph read as a weaver's shuttle handed forward — what is passed ahead of the weave: beforehand, in advance.
mnemonic: The shuttle is already through before the thread arrives — ヨ. 予定, 予約, 天気予報: tomorrow, pre-threaded.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + a phonetic (羕, ヨウ) — the pattern of the grain: manner, appearance; extended into the honorific 〜様.
mnemonic: Every tree's grain flows its own way: its manner — ヨウ. Address people by their grain: 田中様, treated wood-grain-up.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 枼 'thin slats on a tree' (phonetic ヨウ) — the tree's thin green plates: leaves.
mnemonic: Generations (世) budding off the tree in flat green sheets — は. 言葉: words are the leaves the mouth puts out.

etymology: Phono-semantic: mound (阝) + 昜 'sun blazing up' (phonetic ヨウ) — the sunlit south face of the hill: sunshine, the yang principle.
mnemonic: The bright side of the slope, where snow gives up first — ヨウ. 太陽: the source of every south face.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 洛 (phonetic ラク) — leaves letting go one by one: to fall, drop, fail.
mnemonic: Every leaf reaches the same conclusion separately — おちる. 落ち着く is falling until you settle, calm at last.

etymology: Compound: water (氵) + 㐬 — a newborn head-down with hair streaming — carried off by the water: current, to flow.
mnemonic: Hair streaming in the current, everything swept one way — ながれる. Styles, rumors and rivers all 流れる.

etymology: Simplified from 兩: a yoke or scale-beam holding two sides in balance — both; an old coin weighed on such scales.
mnemonic: One beam, two pans, matched — リョウ. 両手, 両親, 両方: hands, parents, sides — the things that come in balanced pairs.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 彔 (phonetic リョク) — silk dyed the color of young growth: green.
mnemonic: Thread pulled from the dye-vat dripping spring color — みどり. The Yamanote line runs on rails of this kanji.

etymology: Simplified from 禮: altar (示) + ritual vessel (豊) — the proper conduct of the rite: etiquette, the bow, thanks.
mnemonic: At the altar, the body folds on the little hook: the bow — レイ. お礼 is that hook offered to a person instead of a god.

etymology: Compound ideograph: bones (歹) laid out in order by the blade (刂) — things arranged in sequence: a row, a file.
mnemonic: The surgeon's tray: everything in its grim, tidy line — レツ. 行列 is the human version: the queue.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 柬 (phonetic レン) — raw silk boiled and worked until supple: to refine; refining yourself: practice.
mnemonic: Boil the silk, work it, boil it again: softness is earned — レン. 練習 does to you what the vat does to thread.

etymology: Phono-semantic: foot (足) + 各 'arrive' (phonetic ロ) — where feet arrive one after another: the road, the route.
mnemonic: Feet arriving in each other's prints until the ground remembers — ロ. 道路 doubles it; 線路 lays it in steel.

etymology: Phono-semantic: grain (禾, phonetic ワ) + mouth (口) — grain shared among mouths: peace, harmony; the name Japan chose for its own style: 和.
mnemonic: Rice enough for every mouth at the table — ワ. 平和 is the treaty; 和食, 和室, 和風: harmony you can eat, sit in, and decorate with.

etymology: Compound: a hand drawing something under cover, the heart (心) held close, feet trailing slow (夂) — walking carefully with a full heart: love.
mnemonic: Carrying a heart so carefully your feet forget to hurry — あい. The kanji walks the way people in love actually walk.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 安 'at ease' (phonetic アン) + wood (木) — the desk one leans on at ease; what is drafted there: a plan, a proposal.
mnemonic: Elbows on the wooden desk, turning the idea over in comfort — アン. 案内 hands your plan to a stranger politely.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (亻) at their standing-place (立) in the court line-up — one's position: rank, grade.
mnemonic: Everyone stands exactly where their title puts them — イ. 一位, 二位: the podium is just this kanji with steps.

etymology: Pictograph: a robe with its crossed collar and trailing hems — clothing. As a component (衤) it dresses kanji like 服's cousins 被 and 裏.
mnemonic: The kimono collar crossing at the throat, hem sweeping the floor — ころも, イ. 衣服: the kanji you put on every day.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand pressing a kneeling figure down — pressing from above: to stamp; the seal so pressed.
mnemonic: Press straight down and hold: the mark takes — しるし, イン. In Japan the 印鑑 outranks your signature.

etymology: Simplified from 榮: torches blazing around a tree in full bloom — splendor, prosperity: to flourish.
mnemonic: A tree lit up like a festival, every branch a lantern — さかえる. 栄光: the tree at maximum wattage.

etymology: Simplified from 鹽: brine worked in pans (皿) on the shore (土) — sea-water boiled down: salt.
mnemonic: Seawater in the flat dish, sun and fire doing the rest: white crystals — しお. The one rock you eat daily.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 意 (phonetic オク) — a number at the edge of what a mind can hold: one hundred million.
mnemonic: A person trying to imagine (意) the crowd: 100,000,000 — オク. Japan counts its population in 億 — barely.

etymology: Compound ideograph: strength (力) added to the voice (口) — piling on: to add, to join.
mnemonic: Push (力) your word (口) onto the pile: +1 — くわえる. 参加 is adding yourself; カナダ borrowed it for its own name: 加奈陀.

etymology: Pictograph: a tree (木) with a round fruit heavy at its top — fruit; what ripens from actions: result.
mnemonic: The tree holds up its finished work — くだもの (果物), the fruit; 結果, the fruit of everything else.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 果 'result' (phonetic カ) — tasks assigned and reckoned by results: a lesson, an administrative section.
mnemonic: Assignments handed out, fruit expected by Friday — カ. 第一課 in the textbook, 課長 at the office: same harvest logic.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 化 'change' (phonetic カ) + money (貝) — goods that change into money and back: wares, freight, currency.
mnemonic: Boxes that are just money in disguise (化) — カ. 貨物 rides the rails; 硬貨 jingles in your pocket.

etymology: Compound ideograph: the self (己) under the correcting hand (攵) — beaten into better shape: to reform, revise.
mnemonic: Take the stick to your own habits — あらためる. 改札 reforms your ticket; 改善 reforms everything else, kaizen.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 戒 'restrain' (phonetic カイ) — originally wooden fetters; any engineered wooden device: a contraption, machinery.
mnemonic: Wood that holds and moves by design: first shackles, then machines — カイ. 機械: the contraption fully grown.

etymology: Compound: under a roof (宀), a gouging instrument (丰) over a mouth (口) — damage done within the house: harm, injury.
mnemonic: The wound happens indoors, where it isn't supposed to — ガイ. 公害, 被害: harm with an address.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a foot (夂) arriving at a doorway (口) — arrivals one at a time: each, respectively.
mnemonic: One visitor at a time crossing the doorstep — カク. 各駅停車: the train that greets each station personally.

etymology: Simplified from 覺: the crown of learning over 見 'see' — seeing with sudden clarity: to awaken; to fix in mind: to memorize.
mnemonic: The lights snap on over your eyes: got it, and I'm keeping it — おぼえる; 目が覚める, the same lights at 7 a.m.
